integrations_researched.name: OpenSSL
integrations_researched.current_usage: Already a dependency - used for MD5, SHA, EVP (digest/crypto functions) in puppet_stdlib.c, puppet_pluginsync.c, and puppetc_server.c

verified_package.name: openssl
verified_package.install_command: apt-get install libssl-dev (Debian/Ubuntu) or pkg-config openssl

key_functions: SSL_CTX_set_verify() - Set client certificate verification mode
X509_sign() - Sign certificate with CA key
PEM_write_X509() - Write certificate to PEM format
PEM_read_X509() - Read certificate from PEM format
api_patterns.verified_against: OpenSSL Wiki SSL/TLS Client documentation, Aticleworld tutorial, FM4DD example code

gotchas: Must call SSL_library_init() and SSL_load_error_strings() before using SSL functions
OpenSSL 3.0+ deprecated some functions - use EVP_* APIs for future compatibility
Certificate verification requires proper CA chain setup
Thread safety requires CRYPTO_set_locking_callback in older versions
Must properly free SSL_CTX and SSL objects to avoid memory leaks

integrations_researched.name: libmicrohttpd
integrations_researched.current_usage: Already a dependency - used for HTTP server in puppetc_server.c

key_functions: MHD_start_daemon() - Start HTTP(S) daemon with MHD_USE_TLS flag

gotchas: CRITICAL: libmicrohttpd ONLY supports GnuTLS for TLS, NOT OpenSSL
This conflicts with the requirement to use OpenSSL and not GnuTLS
MHD_start_daemon returns NULL if compiled without SSL support
SNI support requires GnuTLS 3.0+
OCSP stapling requires GnuTLS 3.6.3+
Priority string is passed directly to gnutls_priority_init()
Android fork replaced GnuTLS with BoringSSL but this is not in upstream

integrations_researched.name: libcurl
integrations_researched.current_usage: Already a dependency - used for HTTP client in puppetc_agent.c

key_functions: curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_SSLKEY, "client-key.pem") - Set client private key
curl_easy_setopt(curl, CURLOPT_CAINFO, "ca.pem") - Set CA certificate for verification

gotchas: Must use libcurl4-openssl-dev package variant (not gnutls variant) to ensure OpenSSL backend
Default certificate verification may fail if system CA bundle is not properly configured
Client certificate and key can be in same file or separate files
CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=1 and CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST=2 are critical for security
Must call curl_global_init() before any other curl functions
Certificate format defaults to PEM but can be changed with CURLOPT_SSLCERTTYPE

integrations_researched.name: Puppet SSL/TLS Implementation

certificate_workflow: 1. Agent generates private key and CSR
2. Agent submits CSR to CA (Puppet Server)
3. CA signs CSR (manually or via autosign)
5. Agent uses certificate for mutual TLS
autosign_methods: naive: autosign = true in puppet.conf [server] section - signs ALL CSRs (INSECURE)
basic: autosign.conf file with whitelist of certnames/domain globs (INSECURE - any host can claim any certname)
policy-based: autosign = /path/to/executable - runs script to validate CSR (RECOMMENDED)

config_files: puppet.conf - Main config with [server] section for autosign setting
autosign.conf - Whitelist for basic autosigning (one certname/glob per line)
autosign executable - Custom policy script for policy-based autosigning

gotchas: Naive autosigning (autosign=true) is INSECURE - should only be used in trusted/isolated networks
Basic autosigning via autosign.conf is also INSECURE - any host can provide any certname
Policy-based autosigning is the recommended secure approach
Puppet best practices recommend using the danieldreier/autosign module for policy-based autosigning
CSRs must be manually signed by default using 'puppetserver ca' command
Autosign policy executable receives CSR on stdin and returns exit code 0 for approval

integrations_researched.name: Docker Certificate Management

approaches: Volume mounts: Mount certificate directory from host into container
Docker secrets: Use Docker Swarm secrets for certificate distribution
Build-time: Copy CA cert and run update-ca-certificates in Dockerfile (for CA trust)
Runtime injection: Use init scripts to generate/copy certificates at container startup
api_patterns.verified_against: Docker documentation and best practices articles

gotchas: NEVER bake private keys/certificates into container images - use volumes or secrets
Certificates added at runtime don't persist if container is destroyed
Different base images have different trust store locations
ca-certificates package is standard but paths may vary across distributions
Docker has proven to be the most difficult environment for certificate automation
Use volume mounts for development, Docker secrets for production
Certificates must be readable by the application user in the container

integrations_researched.name: Debian Package SSL Management

postinst_pattern: Use ssl-cert package utilities for certificate generation
Place certificates in /etc/ssl/certs/ and keys in /etc/ssl/private/
Use deb-systemd-invoke instead of systemctl for service management
Generate certificates in postinst script if they don't exist
api_patterns.verified_against: Debian wiki and ssl-cert package documentation

dependencies: ssl-cert - OpenSSL wrapper for certificate generation

gotchas: ssl-cert package automatically creates self-signed certificate on install
Private keys in /etc/ssl/private/ should have mode 600 or 640
Use ssl-cert group for applications that need to read private keys
postinst scripts should use deb-systemd-invoke not systemctl directly
Certificate generation should be idempotent - only generate if not exists
Consider using debconf for interactive certificate configuration

critical_issues.description: libmicrohttpd only supports GnuTLS for TLS/HTTPS, NOT OpenSSL. The requirements explicitly state 'OpenSSL is already a dependency, so do not use gnutls'.
critical_issues.impact: HIGH - Cannot add TLS to existing server without either: (1) violating requirements by adding GnuTLS, (2) replacing libmicrohttpd with different HTTP server library, or (3) implementing custom SSL socket wrapping
possible_solutions: Solution 1: Add GnuTLS as additional dependency alongside OpenSSL (violates 'do not use gnutls' requirement)
Solution 2: Replace libmicrohttpd with a different HTTP server library that supports OpenSSL (e.g., custom implementation using raw OpenSSL SSL_* APIs)
Solution 3: Use libmicrohttpd without TLS and wrap the socket layer manually with OpenSSL (complex, error-prone)
Solution 4: Use Android's BoringSSL fork of libmicrohttpd (unmaintained, non-upstream)
Solution 5: Implement custom HTTP server using OpenSSL BIO/SSL APIs directly
critical_issues.recommendation: Consult with project stakeholders to clarify requirements. If OpenSSL-only is firm requirement, recommend Solution 2 (custom HTTP server implementation) or Solution 5 (replace libmicrohttpd). If GnuTLS is acceptable for server-side only while using OpenSSL for agent-side and certificate operations, Solution 1 is simplest.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Resolve libmicrohttpd/GnuTLS vs OpenSSL conflict before implementation
For agent (client) side: libcurl with OpenSSL backend is ready to use - ensure libcurl4-openssl-dev is installed (not gnutls variant)
Implement certificate generation and signing using OpenSSL X509/EVP APIs in C
Follow Puppet's certificate workflow: agent generates CSR -> submits to server -> server signs -> agent retrieves
Implement all three autosign modes (naive, basic, policy-based) matching Puppet behavior
Store CA certificate and key on server side only; distribute CA certificate to agents
Use /etc/puppetc/ssl/ directory structure similar to Puppet's ssldir
For Docker: Use volume mounts for certificate directories, never bake certs into images
For Debian packaging: Use ssl-cert utilities in postinst script to generate initial CA if not exists
Consider security: Default to manual CSR signing (no autosign), warn users about autosign security implications
Implement proper certificate validation: verify CA chain, check expiration, validate CN/SAN
